scope: Observed fetched-opcode histogram at broad-census unsupported cuts and conditional-Jcc successor cuts; pinned Windows 3.11 60M and lean stock xv6 forktest

validation.focusedTests: 17/17 pass, including prefix, fetched group extension, refusal partitions, unchanged prior counters and guest parity
validation.existingCounters: Both full workloads have byte-identical unlinked mode and Jcc-linked objects compared with the preceding census. For every mode, the primary and canonical-prefix histograms each partition unsupported-opcode plus unsupported-0f first refusals; 0F second-byte histograms partition unsupported-0f. Jcc successor counterparts partition the corresponding link refusals. Group-extension buckets are subsets, not additive totals.

vm86.interpretation: Segment reload and stack/segment operations dominate these mode cuts; opcode counts are not a safe executable block contract.

interpretation: Missing successor cuts concentrate in different small syntax sets: Windows protected16 3A/3C account for 639,438 of 993,765 unsupported Jcc successors, and xv6 protected32 25/F6 /0 account for 1,026,475 of 1,155,632. FF is mixed: its /2, /4, /0 and other extensions have different control/data semantics. This histogram justifies a later opt-in syntactic grammar trial, not an inferred coverage increment, native safety proof or speed claim. No grammar or guest execution changed in this experiment.
